text:
maria.dev: Heads-up — I want to provision a small GPU nodepool in us-central1 for a staging inference workload (low qps, tight p99). Thinking a T4-based pool for cost, or an A2 (A100) single-gpu flavor for parity with prod. Need input on sizing, autoscaler settings, quota requests, and egress/NAT considerations.

alex.infra: +1. For staging i'd prefer T4 (nvidia-tesla-t4) to keep costs down. If you need the exact fp16 speed of A100 we should mirror prod but smaller. What's your expected pod concurrency and max sequence length?

maria.dev: Mostly single-conversation gen, bursty. Max parallel pods ~12, typically 2-4. Seq len ~512. Latency SLO ~200ms p95.

jon.sre: If target is p95 200ms, T4 is ok if we keep small batch sizes and tight node autoscale. Suggest nodepool: min=0 max=4, nodes with 1 GPU each, and cluster-autoscaler balance-similar-node-groups=false? Also taint nodes: gpu=true:NoSchedule and add a GPU toleration to pods.

alex.infra: Agree on taints. Also set scale-down-unneeded-time to 2m so they don't stay up during short bursts. But be careful with too aggressive scale-down if your model has cold-start overhead (CUDA init).

maria.dev: Good points. Any comments on preemptible/spot nodes vs standard? Want to save cost but avoid noisy evictions during tests.

jon.sre: For staging we can use spot nodes with a fallback pool of 1 standard node for critical jobs. Use pod priorities so important pods survive. If you rely on CUDA context warm starts, evictions will hurt latency tests — consider keeping at least one standard node.

kevin.finance: Rough cost check: T4 on GKE preemptible ~= $0.20/hr, non-preemptible ~$0.50/hr per GPU node (ballpark). 4-node steady-state non-preemptible is ~ $1.9k/mo. We can refine after exact machine types and network egress. :money_with_wings:

sam.ops: Also check our VPC NAT egress quotas — staging projects sometimes hit ephemeral port exhaustion when scaling many nodes/pods. If you have heavy model downloads or callouts we should route through a central NAT with enough routes. See console quotas: https://console.cloud.google.com/iam-admin/quotas

maria.dev: Good call on NAT. The pods will pull model artifacts from internal object storage on startup (~2GB per pod). Could that cause ephemeral port issues?

alex.infra: Yes, parallel downloads from all nodes can exhaust ephemeral ports. Mitigations: stagger startup, pre-populate node-local cache (DaemonSet), or use GCS signed URLs via a shared proxy that limits concurrency. Node-local caching plus small pre-warm cron works well.

jon.sre: For quota - before creating the pool, open a quota ticket for GPU (compute.googleapis.com/GPUS) in us-central1. Also double-check CPU and IP address quotas for the node machine type. I can draft the request.

maria.dev: If we go T4, what's the gcloud command to create the pool?

alex.infra: Example:

```
gcloud container node-pools create gpu-staging-t4 \  --cluster=redwood-staging --region=us-central1 \  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-t4,count=1 \  --num-nodes=1 \  --enable-autoscaling --min-nodes=0 --max-nodes=4 \  --node-taints=gpu=true:NoSchedule \  --workload-metadata=GKE_METADATA_SERVER
```

alex.infra: After creation, install the NVIDIA device-plugin and node-feature-discovery if not present.

jon.sre: I'll open the quota ticket and include expected numbers: 4 GPUs in us-central1 initially, CPU quota bump to match nodes, and 50 static external IPs removed — we prefer NAT. I'll post the ticket id when I have it.

infra-bot: [deploy-bot] Node pool creation requested by alex.infra for cluster redwood-staging. Status: pending.

maria.dev: Thanks — can we also pin the nodepool to a single zone (us-central1-b) to reduce cross-zone egress? Or prefer regional for AZ resilience?

jon.sre: For staging single-zone is fine and cheaper network-wise, but note node autoscaler behaves per-zone. If you need resilience, make it regional and set max nodes per zone conservatively.

kevin.finance: When you finalize machine types and hours estimate, ping me and I’ll run a quick TCO calc and approve a staging cost bucket.

maria.dev: Awesome — @jon.sre please paste the quota ticket id and @alex.infra please create the node-pool when ticket is approved. I'll add startup stagger and a node-prepull DaemonSet. :thumbsup:

jon.sre: Ticket created: https://console.cloud.google.com/support/cases/123456789 (GPU quota request for us-central1, 4 T4 GPUs). Will update here when approved.

sam.ops: FYI — adding NAT gateway capacity for ephemeral ports may need a support escalation. If ticket stalls ping me.

maria.dev: Thanks everyone. I'll wait for the quota approval then kick this off.
